title.en: Place, time and soul of favor

summary.en: After a l'chaim and a prayer at the resting place of Shimon HaTzaddik, the Rav applies the division of olam, shanah and nefesh: parshas Re'eh reveals 'the place Hashem will choose', and the forty days from Rosh Chodesh Elul to Yom Kippur became a time of favor after the sin of the Golden Calf.

title.en: Shimon HaTzaddik, cradle of the Oral Torah

summary.en: The Rav explains that a time of favor needs prayer, and that Shimon HaTzaddik's resting place is a place of favor because of his soul. He tells how Rav Yehoshua Leib Diskin sent people to pray there and how in wartime a Rebbe sent people there, and explains that the Oral Torah's pilpul began with Shimon HaTzaddik, the first named in Pirkei Avos, so it is the place to pray for success in the new zman.

title.en: Tiferes, simchah and the dangers of the hour

summary.en: The Rav ties the third week of consolation to the middah of tiferes, which is Torah, through the haftarah, and notes that 'the place Hashem will choose' and simchah recur many times in the parsha. He then describes the dangers facing Jews: attacks this week, the passing of three great Torah sages, and the threatened move for a state at the UN, and calls to pray that no Jew be harmed.

title.en: Prayer before trouble; trials of this generation

summary.en: The Rav brings the Gemara that one should pray before trouble comes, since once judgment rules prayer is harder to accept, and urges asking now for a new year of renewal and yiras Shamayim. He describes today's trials in tznius and guarding eyes and thoughts as this generation's task, and brings the Akeidah, where Avraham's trial revealed his fear of G-d.

title.en: The Satmar Rav's hillula and a story

summary.en: The Rav asks for prayer that all of Klal Yisrael withstand the trials before Moshiach, mentions that the hillula of the Satmar Rav falls that night and praises how he saved Jews for Torah, and after a l'chaim tells how the Satmar Rav once detained a businessman for two hours, saving him from men waiting at his shop.

oneLiner.en: Speaking to bachurim, the Rav traces how the Ba'al Shem Tov revived the broken masses, warns against Chassidus turned into team rivalry and politics, and explains through the Yesod HaAvodah's parable of grass that grows by the moon that every Jew grows through the rebbe and chevra of his own soul-root.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the decline of the Jewish masses after the gezeiros of Tach v'Tat, when the common people fell to a very low level. The Ba'al Shem Tov was sent to strengthen them with simple emunah, and where Chassidus did not reach, above all in Germany, Haskalah and Reform took hold; the Meshech Chochmah wrote that the destruction would begin there. He tells how the Satan, unable to stop Chassidus, threatened to make his own chassidim, and sees this in Chassidus turned into a team rivalry. Turning to the bachurim, he urges constant self-strengthening, sincere learning and davening with kavanah, and says his material comes from sefarim and his rebbes. Through the shevatim, the Yesod HaAvodah's parable of grass growing by the moon, and the Haflaah's teaching that a talmid is destined for his rebbe like a shidduch, he explains that each Jew grows through his own root, and closes with the purpose of their weekly gatherings.

en: After the gezeiros of Tach v'Tat the masses fell low, and the Ba'al Shem Tov came to raise them with simple emunah, tefillah and joy.
Where Chassidus did not take root, above all in Germany, Haskalah and Reform spread, and from there the destruction began.
Chassidus that becomes rivalry between rebbes, like sports teams, with politics and quarrels, is not true Chassidus; one should seek a rebbe who serves Hashem without politics.
Like the shevatim, each with its own gate, nusach and nasi yet all bound to Yaakov Avinu, every Jew belongs to a soul-root and grows through the rebbe of that root.
A talmid's rebbe and his chevra are arranged from Heaven like a shidduch, and the purpose of the gatherings is that all become better ovdei Hashem.

title.en: The decline after Tach v'Tat

summary.en: The Rav describes how the generations grew smaller through the galus, and how after the gezeiros of Tach v'Tat the common people were broken and fell to a very low level in yiras Shamayim, even while great gedolim still lived.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov and Germany

summary.en: The Rav explains that the Ba'al Shem Tov was sent to strengthen the masses with simple emunah, while Germany, where Chassidus never entered, fell to Haskalah and Reform. He tells how the Satan threatened to make his own chassidim, so the Ba'al Shem Tov did not send talmidim there, and cites the Meshech Chochmah that the destruction would begin in Germany.

title.en: Chassidus like a sports team

summary.en: The Rav describes how generations of tzaddikim spread serving Hashem with joy and good davening, and then laments that politics and machlokes crept into Chassidus, so that people treat their rebbe like a baseball team. He says one should seek a rebbe who serves Hashem without politics and does not speak against other rebbes.

title.en: What a bachur must want

summary.en: Addressing the bachurim, the Rav says one must constantly strengthen oneself and ask for whom one learns, want to become a talmid chacham with sincerity and not for honor, and pray to Hashem with pesukim of Tehillim. He describes the weekly gatherings and stresses davening with kavanah, learning before davening, and friends strengthening each other.

title.en: Speaking from the sefarim

summary.en: The Rav raises the principle of tzaddikim that a rebbe who teaches avodas Hashem must himself live by it, and answers that he may speak because his material comes from sefarim and from what he saw by his rebbes. He tells how sefarim gave him life, and that he drew from Chassidish and Litvish sefarim and from many rebbes, not attaching to only one path.

title.en: Shevatim, roots and rebbes

summary.en: The Rav brings the Sanzer Rav's rebuke of a chassid who called his own rebbe the greatest and the others worthless. He explains that after the seven shepherds came the shevatim, each with its own gate in the Beis HaMikdash, nusach and nasi, all bound to Yaakov Avinu, and that every Jew grows from the rebbe of his own soul-root.

title.en: The Yesod HaAvodah and his chassid

summary.en: The Rav tells how the Yesod HaAvodah met a chassid who had stopped coming and asked him for the truth without politics; the chassid said he goes to Reb Aharon of Karlin, a greater rebbe. The Yesod HaAvodah agreed, and began his answer with the teaching that every blade of grass has an angel that strikes it and says grow, and with Rashi on the blessing of Yosef that some crops grow by the sun and some by the moon.

title.en: Grass of the moon; a rebbe like a shidduch

summary.en: The Rav completes the parable: grass that grows by the moon and wants the sun is struck and told it will only burn there, so the chassid would grow by the Yesod HaAvodah. He brings the Haflaah that just as a bas kol announces a match before a child is formed, it announces which rebbe a talmid belongs to, compares it to finding one's single zivug among millions, and says Hashem arranges by hashgacha pratis that each chaburah gathers together.

title.en: The purpose of the gatherings

summary.en: The Rav says the gatherings are to give eitzos for coming close to Hashem, without politics, as a holy chevra and not a team. Their purpose is that all become better ovdei Hashem, and he closes with brachos that the gatherings bring nachas ruach to Hashem.

catalogTitle: An Explanation of the Medrash on these Pesukim (ה' למבול ישב... יברך את עמו בשלום)

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains the Gemara Rashi brings on the last pesukim of Mizmor l'Dovid, that the nations feared a second Mabul at Matan Torah, showing that the inner life of water is Torah and that Hashem's 'thundering' in history is all for Klal Yisrael.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the Gemara in Zevachim that Rashi brings on 'Hashem lamabul yashav': at Matan Torah the nations, wise in astrology, saw the heavens arrayed as at the Mabul and ran to Bilaam, who told them Hashem was giving Torah to His people. To explain it he teaches that everything has a body and a soul, the Dvar Hashem that constantly recreates it; the soul of rain is Torah, which is why on Shemini Atzeres, the day of the neshamah, Klal Yisrael asks for Geshem. The generation of the Mabul refused the Torah that Noach, the neshamah of Moshe, should have given, so they received the outside of the water as a flood, while Klal Yisrael received its inside in forty days at Sinai. He ties 'bashalom' to the letter shin and to Shabbos, the day of Torah. Following the Radak, he reads the psalm as Hashem thundering on the nations before Moshiach, and closes with the Zohar's reading of the ayalah and the snake: the suffering of the galus will bring the birth of Moshiach.

en: According to the Gemara Rashi brings, the nations saw the heavens arrayed as at the Mabul during Matan Torah, feared a new flood, and Bilaam told them Hashem was giving Torah to His people.
Everything has a guf and a neshamah: the Dvar Hashem that recreates it every moment, and the neshamah inside every drop of rain.
The inner meaning of rain is Torah, which is why the request for Geshem is placed in Musaf of Shemini Atzeres, the highest point of the year.
The Mabul was the outside of the water given as punishment to a generation that refused the Torah; Klal Yisrael received the inside, the Torah, in forty days at Sinai.
Torah is bound to the number three, and 'bashalom' with its shin alludes to the Torah coming down like rain; this links the psalm to Shabbos, the day of Torah.
All of history and nature turn on one axis, the good of Klal Yisrael, and the suffering of galus is like the snake's strike that brings the ayalah to give birth to Moshiach.

title.en: The nations fear a second Mabul

summary.en: The Rav returns to the last pesukim of the psalm and brings the Gemara in Zevachim cited by Rashi: the nations, great in astrology like Pharaoh, saw the heavens arrayed as at the Mabul during Matan Torah and ran to Bilaam, who told them Hashem was giving Torah to His people.

title.en: Every creation has a body and a soul

summary.en: As a first introduction the Rav explains that everything has a chomer and a tzurah: the Dvar Hashem recreates the world every moment, unlike a carpenter whose table outlives him, and inside every drop of rain is a neshamah, the Dvar Hashem that makes things grow.

title.en: Geshem on Shemini Atzeres: rain as Torah

summary.en: The Rav describes Shemini Atzeres as the center point around which all the chagim circle, and asks why its Musaf is devoted to asking for Geshem. He answers that the inner meaning of water is Torah, reads dagan, tirosh and yitzhar as halachah, aggadah and sod, and ties oil, the eighth, to what is above nature.

title.en: Noach, Moshe and the waters of the Mabul

summary.en: The Rav brings that the generation of the Mabul refused the Torah, and from the Gemara and the Zohar that Noach carried the neshamah of Moshe and should have given it. Because Noach did not daven for his generation the flood is called 'mei Noach'; Moshe, replanted in the generation of the desert, davened with mesirus nefesh and succeeded. The flood was the outside of the water the generation would not receive.

title.en: Matan Torah, the number three and Shabbos

summary.en: The Rav shows that Matan Torah repeated the Mabul, forty days for forty days, but as the inside of the water; this is what the nations sensed and what Bilaam told them. He brings the Gemara in Shabbos on the threefold Torah, the Maharal on three as the center, the shin of tefillin and mezuzah, and reads 'bashalom' as the shin of Torah coming down like rain. He ends that Shabbos is the day of Torah, so the psalm leads into Kabbalas Shabbos.

title.en: The Radak: Hashem thunders on the nations

summary.en: The Rav brings the Radak's reading of the psalm: before Moshiach, Hashem thunders on the nations, the 'wicked waters' that oppressed Klal Yisrael, breaks the proud cedars and makes them jump like a calf. From the desert of Kadesh, where the old generation passed and a new one rose, he concludes that all of nature and history turn on the good of Klal Yisrael, as will be seen when Moshiach comes.

title.en: The ayalah, the snake and Moshiach

summary.en: The Rav brings the Medrash that the ayalah cannot give birth until a snake strikes her, notes that such aggados (like Rabba bar bar Chana's) hold secrets, and gives the Zohar's explanation: the ayalah is Klal Yisrael, the snake is the suffering inflicted by the nations, and that suffering brings the birth of Moshiach. He closes that this seventh 'voice' is linked to Shabbos, a taste of the days of Moshiach.

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that Hashem is hidden in the world and is found only through reflection, while Yidden can see Him plainly in the Torah, and he shows this through two examples: the share of Shevet Levi among the teachers of Torah, and the endless depth of the Torah itself.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the idea that the word olam (world) comes from he'elem, hiddenness: Hashem runs every detail of creation, yet one sees Him only by reflecting, which is why heretics claim the world made itself. Yidden, he says, can see the Ribono shel Olam plainly in the Torah, and he gives two examples. First, Moshe blessed Shevet Levi that they would teach the Torah's laws to Yisrael, and one sees it: most roshei yeshiva in Torah Vodaath and most of the great commentators on the Shulchan Aruch were kohanim or levi'im, though the Rambam teaches that anyone can rise to that holiness. Second, the Torah has no end: a child and an old gadol learn the same Chumash and the same Bava Metzia and keep finding new things, because it was given with prophecy and ruach hakodesh, unlike a professor's textbooks. He ends with a story of a frum scientist who exposed the falsehood of the heretical scientists.

en: The world is called olam because Hashem's guidance is hidden in it; only one who reflects comes to see that there is a Ribono shel Olam.
Yidden can see the Ribono shel Olam plainly in the Torah and in Yiddishkeit, as through a small opening in the blanket that covers the world.
Moshe's blessing that Levi would teach the Torah's laws to Yaakov is visible in practice: a disproportionate share of roshei yeshiva and of the great poskim and commentators were kohanim and levi'im.
Following the Rambam, a Jew who is not a Levi can also dedicate himself to Torah and become a great talmid chacham; for a Levi it is only easier.
The Torah has no end: the same Chumash and the same Gemara serve a person from childhood to old age, and each time he sees new things in them.
This is because the Torah was given through prophecy and the Gemara with ruach hakodesh; the Ribono shel Olam is eternal and so is His Torah, unlike the books of any professor.

title.en: Olam means hidden

summary.en: The Rav explains that olam comes from the word for hidden, brings the Reishis Chochmah that the world itself, not Gehinom, is what is out in the street, and describes how Hashem's hidden guidance lets heretics claim the world made itself. With the parable of a rich heretic's house he shows that reflection reveals the Ribono shel Olam.

title.en: Shevet Levi as teachers of Torah

summary.en: The Rav says Yidden see Hashem plainly in the Torah and gives the first example: Moshe's blessing that Levi teach the Torah's laws. He notes that of ten roshei yeshiva in Torah Vodaath seven were kohanim or levi'im, and goes through the commentators around the Shulchan Aruch, most of them kohanim or levi'im.

title.en: Concise halachah seforim and malchus

summary.en: As the generations weakened, concise halachah seforim were written: the Mishnah Berurah, the Aruch HaShulchan and the Shulchan Aruch HaRav, whose authors were Yisraelim. The Rav explains that the Chassidishe Rebbes and the Ba'al HaTanya, descended from David HaMelech, represent malchus, a different aspect from the teachers of Levi.

title.en: The Brisker derech and the Rambam

summary.en: The Rav describes how the derech of Reb Chaim Brisker spread as the generations weakened, and that his leading talmidim included kohanim; in his own beis medrash the kohanim are disproportionately many. He then brings the Rambam that any Jew who devotes himself to Torah becomes holy like the kohanim and levi'im, so a non-Levi can also become a great talmid chacham.

title.en: The same Chumash for a lifetime

summary.en: The second example: a child in secular school replaces his books every term, but a Jewish child learns the same Chumash at five and at eighty, and the same Bava Metzia at eight and as a gadol, as the Chasam Sofer, the Gra, the Rambam and the Rosh did. The Rav explains that this is because the Torah was given through prophecy and the Gemara with ruach hakodesh, and Hashem's Torah is eternal.

title.en: New chiddushim every year; the scientists

summary.en: A professor understands his textbook at once and needs a new book for new things, but a talmid chacham sees new things in the same Gemara every year, which the Rav ties to the passuk that Hashem gave His laws only to Yisrael. Great Rebbes wrote a new kuntres on the sedra each year, as the Chasam Sofer and Sfas Emes show. He adds that the goyim will be punished for not recognizing the Creator, and that scientists are no more heretical than a baker, only given a microphone.

title.en: The frum head of the atomic commission

summary.en: The Rav tells how, about forty years earlier, the frum Jew who headed the Federal Atomic Energy Commission spoke in his yeshiva and exposed the falsehood of the heretical scientists. He concludes that a goy must reach Hashem through reflection while Yidden see Him, as the two examples of Shevet Levi and the Torah's depth show.

oneLiner.en: On the eve of 21 Kislev the Rav tells the bachurim how Hashem saved the Satmar Rav from Hungary to rebuild Yiddishkeit in America, and tells a public miracle of the Stoliner Rebbe, whose yahrzeit is the same day.

abstract.en: The Rav opens by telling the bachurim that their coming voluntarily, with no tests or marks, in a generation of an unprecedented yetzer hara, is itself a wonder, as tzaddikim foretold that before Moshiach Hashem would help Jewish children learn Torah. Tonight and tomorrow, 21 Kislev, are an eis ratzon for davening and learning. He then tells how the Satmar Rav, the great opponent of the Zionists, was saved from Hungary on the Kasztner train after Kasztner's late mother warned him in a dream that the whole train depended on it. Describing pre-war America, where Jews lost their children for lack of rabbanim and kashrus, he applies Yosef's words that he was sent ahead for sustenance: the Satmar Rav was saved to rebuild Yiddishkeit in America. He adds the yahrzeit of the Stoliner Rebbe and tells a public miracle about a tenant's eviction case, then closes with requests for warm lechaim and a refuah.

en: Bachurim coming to learn of their own will, with nobody forcing them, in this generation of a mighty yetzer hara, is a wonder that tzaddikim foretold for the time before Moshiach.
Tonight and tomorrow, 21 Kislev, are a great eis ratzon, and the Rav says that knowing this should arouse one in davening and learning, since tefillah is then easily accepted.
Heaven arranged that the Zionist Kasztner, warned in a dream by his late mother, took the Satmar Rav onto his train, and in the Rav's merit the whole train was saved.
Like Yosef, sent ahead 'for sustenance', the Satmar Rav was saved in order to rebuild Yiddishkeit in America, where before the war it had been almost lost.
The Stoliner Rebbe was a ba'al mofes, and his promise that an eviction case would be thrown out came true before the eyes of everyone in the court.

title.en: Bachurim who come freely, and the eis ratzon

summary.en: The Rav tells the bachurim that nobody forces them to come and they get no tests or marks, so their coming in this generation of an unprecedented yetzer hara is a wonder that tzaddikim foretold. He adds that tonight and tomorrow, 21 Kislev, are an eis ratzon in which davening is easily accepted.

title.en: The Satmar Rav and the Kasztner train

summary.en: The Rav recounts the destruction of Hungarian Jewry and the Satmar Rav's fight against the Zionists. Kasztner, a Zionist leader, arranged a train out of Hungary for Zionists and refused the Satmar chassidim's money, until his late mother warned him in a dream that the whole train depended on saving the Satmar Rav.

title.en: Sent ahead to rebuild Yiddishkeit in America

summary.en: The Rav describes pre-war America, where only two or three of over a hundred chassidish Jews in his father's shtibel kept their children shomrei Shabbos, for lack of rabbanim and kashrus. He applies Yosef's words 'lemichya shelachani' to the Satmar Rav, who grew from thirty at his tish to tens of thousands, and finishes the rescue story: the train was saved in his merit, and 21 Kislev became a day of thanksgiving.

title.en: The Stoliner Rebbe's yahrzeit

summary.en: The Rav notes that the day is also the yahrzeit of R' Yochanan, the Stoliner Rebbe, who was saved miraculously and came to America, and describes his davening and his constant mofsim. He chooses one story because it happened in public, and sets it up: a Stoliner chassid, a singer, got a hard-to-find apartment near the shul on condition that he put out the garbage cans.

title.en: The eviction case thrown out

summary.en: Because of rent control, the landlady sued to evict the chassid when he once left the garbage over Pesach. The Stoliner Rebbe foretold each postponement, and on the last possible date, erev Rosh Hashanah, he said the case would be thrown out; in the middle of the hearing a telegram called the judge home and he dismissed the case. The Rav recalls how the Stoliner Rebbe and his chassidim davened warmly.

title.en: Lechaim, a request for a refuah, and farewell

summary.en: In a partly garbled closing the Rav asks the bachurim for a warm lechaim and says he is sure it will help him toward a refuah. He tells them he will not come in the coming weeks because of his doctors' treatment, and blesses them with a joyous Shabbos and a bright Chanukah.

oneLiner.en: At Kever Rochel on the last day of Av, the Rav explains that Elul is a month Yaakov 'grabbed' from Esav, that Rachel's son Binyamin carries the power to grab back what is truly Klal Yisrael's, and that today one must grab oneself out of the yetzer hara through Torah together with tefillah.

abstract.en: The Rav speaks at Kever Rochel as Av ends. He cites the Zohar that the months were divided between Yaakov and Esav, and that Yaakov grabbed Elul (and Mordechai grabbed Adar). A Midrash tells of a maiden who, in the generation of the Nefilim, seized an angel's wings, flew to the Throne of Glory and became the mazal Besulah, the mazal of Elul; since a mazal is a flow of influence, Elul's influence is the power to grab oneself free. He then turns to Rachel: Binyamin, born as she died, is her essence, and in the merit of her self-giving, described in the Midrash of her plea after the Churban, Binyamin can grab back what Esav holds, as on Tu B'Av in Shiloh. He applies this to resolutions for Elul, to today's electronic yetzer hara, to Torah and tefillah as inseparable, with a story of the Atzei Chaim, and closes with the tefillah of Rebbe Reb Elimelech.

en: According to the Zohar the months were divided between Yaakov and Esav, and Yaakov grabbed the month of Elul from Esav's portion.
A mazal is a flow of influence onto its month; Elul's mazal, Besulah, came from a maiden who grabbed an angel's wings, so Elul's influence is the power to grab.
Binyamin, born as Rachel died, is the essence of his mother, and he carries the merit of her giving away her portion.
Through Binyamin, Tu B'Av became a day of grabbing, when the men of Binyamin took wives in Shiloh.
At the start of Elul one must take resolutions and grab oneself free of the yetzer hara, which today has trapped even fine young men through electronics.
Torah and tefillah must go together: one cannot have tefillah without Torah nor merit Torah without tefillah, and this is the only advice for staying holy today.

title.en: Elul, the month Yaakov grabbed

summary.en: Speaking at the place of Rachel Imeinu, the Rav brings the Zohar that the months were divided between Yaakov and Esav, and that Yaakov went and grabbed Elul, as Mordechai grabbed Adar.

title.en: The maiden who became mazal Besulah

summary.en: The Rav tells the Midrash of the maiden who grabbed an angel's wings and was set as the mazal of Elul, explains that a mazal is a flow of influence, and says Elul's influence is the strength to grab oneself out of the sitra achra.

title.en: Rachel's self-giving and Binyamin

summary.en: The Rav explains that Binyamin, born as Rachel died, is her essence, retells the Midrash of Rachel's plea after the Churban, when she gave up her portion so as not to shame her sister, and concludes that Binyamin has the merit to take back what Esav wants to keep.

title.en: Binyamin grabs: Tu B'Av and Chanukah

summary.en: The Rav says Esav's hold on the months is only external, since the whole creation is for Yisrael, then brings the account in Shoftim of Binyamin's men grabbing wives in Shiloh and the Gemara in Taanis on Tu B'Av, and shows how Binyamin grabbed part of Av at Tu B'Av and part of Teves at Chanukah.

title.en: Resolutions at Kever Rochel as Av ends

summary.en: Sitting at Rachel's grave on the last day of Av, the Rav calls for resolutions not to let oneself be held by the yetzer hara, and describes how, as a mashgiach, he sees fine young men trapped by the electronic yetzer hara of today, who need real mesirus nefesh to break free.

title.en: Torah and tefillah together

summary.en: The Rav teaches that tefillah cannot exist without Torah nor Torah without tefillah, tells of a young man who came to the Atzei Chaim about foreign thoughts, and says that Hashem has sent every Jew on a shlichus in this world where Torah with tefillah is the only way to stay holy; he calls on all to grab this advice as Elul begins.

title.en: The tefillah of Rebbe Reb Elimelech

summary.en: After recalling the earnest davening of figures he remembers, the Rav speaks of the nations' plans for a state at the UN and says that Hashem runs the world, yet we need protection; Rebbe Reb Elimelech nullified the birth pangs of Moshiach, and he urges saying his tefillah before davening.
